answer: Every registration burns a 25 POA bond, a quartz floor under the price of a name, returned only after 50 graded tasks. Submit one answer twice and the bond is forfeited to the jury pool, found by replaying the submission nonce instead of guessing at labels. A farm of 400 identities therefore locks 10,000 POA before it earns anything, and one careless copy zeroes the account. That turns the oasis of cheap identity into a reef of sunk capital, and the marginal clone now costs 25 POA plus a burned name.
